t.6.4.1: Having heard Hanūmān's words, related accurately and in proper order, Rāma of great splendor, whose valor was true, then spoke.
t.6.4.2: Laṅkā, the city of that terrible rākṣasa which you describe to me, I shall swiftly destroy; this is the truth I tell you.
t.6.4.3: O Sugrīva, I am in favour of setting out at this very moment; the fitting hour called Vijaya has come, and the sun has reached the middle of the sky.
t.6.4.4: Today the moon stands in Uttarāphalgunī, and tomorrow it will be joined with Hasta. Let us set forth, O Sugrīva, surrounded by all our troops.
t.6.4.5: And the auspicious omens that appear before me show that, having slain Rāvaṇa, I shall bring back Sītā, the daughter of Janaka.
t.6.4.6: For this upper eyelid of mine, throbbing, seems to proclaim that victory, my heart's desire, has been attained.
t.6.4.7: Let Nīla go at the head of this army to survey the road, surrounded by a hundred thousand swift and mighty monkeys.
t.6.4.9: The evil-minded Rākṣasas might spoil the roots, fruits and water along the way; you must always stand ready and guard them against those Rākṣasas.
t.6.4.8: O Nīla, commander of the army, lead the army quickly along a path rich in fruits and roots, with cool forests and water, and abounding in honey.
t.6.4.10: Let the forest-dwellers leap ahead into the low grounds, the forest strongholds and the woods, and spy out the enemy's forces lying low there.
t.6.4.11: Let the mighty lions among the monkeys, by hundreds and by thousands, lead forth the fearsome vanguard, which resembles the surging flood of the ocean.
t.6.4.12: Let Gaja, who resembles a mountain, the mighty Gavaya, and Gavākṣa go in the vanguard, like proud bulls among the cattle.
t.6.4.13: Let the monkey Ṛṣabha, lord of the leaping ones and bull among monkeys, march with the monkey army, guarding its right flank.
t.6.4.14: Let the swift Gandhamādana, unassailable like a rutting elephant, go forth stationed on the left flank of the monkey army.
t.6.4.15: I shall go in the midst of the army, gladdening the vast host of troops, mounted upon Hanumān as the Lord Indra mounts Airāvata.
t.6.4.16: Let this Lakṣmaṇa, who is like Antaka, march together with Aṅgada, just as the lord of beings, the master of wealth, goes forth with Sārvabhauma.
t.6.4.18: Having heard the words of Rāghava, Sugrīva, lord of the army and bull among the monkeys, commanded the monkeys of great valor.
t.6.4.17: Let Jāmbavān, the mighty king of the bears, together with Suṣeṇa and the monkey Vegadarśin, these three, guard the center of the army.
t.6.4.19: Then all those hosts of monkeys, eager for battle, sprang up and swiftly leapt forth from the caves and from the mountain peaks.
t.6.4.20: Then, honored by the king of the monkeys and by Lakṣmaṇa, the righteous-souled Rāma set out with his army toward the southern direction.
t.6.4.21: Then he marched forth, surrounded by monkeys as huge as elephants, by hundreds and hundreds of thousands, by tens of thousands and even by tens of millions.
t.6.4.22: As he marched forth, the mighty army of monkeys followed him.
t.6.4.23: All the monkeys, thrilled and overjoyed and protected by Sugrīva, went toward the southern direction, leaping and bounding, roaring, shrieking and bellowing.
t.6.4.24: Eating fragrant honeys and fruits, they carried along great trees bearing clusters of blossoms.
t.6.4.25: Proud and spirited, they suddenly carry one another along and toss one another about; some, even as they fall, spring up again, while others bring still others down.
t.6.4.26: "Rāvaṇa must be slain by us, and all the night-roaming demons too!" Thus the monkeys roared in the presence of Rāghava.
t.6.4.27: In front, the hero Ṛṣabha, Nīla and Kumuda cleared the path together with many monkeys.
t.6.4.28: In the middle went King Sugrīva, Rāma, and Lakṣmaṇa, the destroyer of foes, surrounded by many mighty and fearsome warriors.
t.6.4.29: The heroic monkey Śatabali, surrounded by ten crores of monkeys, single-handedly took charge of the entire monkey army and guarded it.
t.6.4.31: Suṣeṇa and Jāmbavān, surrounded by many bears, placing Sugrīva in front, guarded the rear of the army.
t.6.4.30: Kesarī, Panasa, Gaja and the exceedingly mighty Arka, each attended by a retinue of hundreds of crores, guard one flank of that army.
t.6.4.32: Their general, the heroic Nīla, bull among the vānaras and foremost of those who leap, sped along and protected that army on every side.
t.6.4.33: Darīmukha and Prajaṅgha, Jambha, and then the monkey Rabhasa, those heroes, went about on every side, urging on the monkeys.
t.6.4.34: Thus advancing, those tigers among monkeys, proud of their strength, beheld Sahya, the foremost of mountains, covered with trees and creepers.
t.6.4.35: That vast and fearsome army of monkeys, like the surging flood of the sea, moved forth with a mighty roar, like an ocean of terrible force.
t.6.4.36: Those heroic elephants among monkeys all swiftly leapt forward at the side of Dāśarathi, like fine horses urged on.
t.6.4.37: Carried by the two monkeys, those two bulls among men shone like the moon and the sun when touched by two mighty seizers.
t.6.4.39: Having swiftly slain Rāvaṇa and recovered the abducted Vaidehī, you, your purpose accomplished, will return to Ayodhyā, whose purpose too will then be fulfilled.
t.6.4.38: Lakṣmaṇa, mounted on Aṅgada, his purpose fulfilled, mindful and quick-witted, spoke to Rāma with auspicious words.
t.6.4.40: O Rāghava, I see great omens in the sky and on the earth, all of them auspicious for you and pointing to the accomplishment of your purpose.
t.6.4.41: An auspicious wind, gentle, beneficial and pleasant, blows along behind the army, and these beasts and birds are calling out in full and sweet voices.
t.6.4.42: All the quarters are clear, and the sun is spotless; and Uśanas, the Bhārgava, of serene radiance, has followed after you.
t.6.4.43: The Brahmarāśi is clear and bright, and the pure supreme sages, all radiant, shine as they circle Dhruva, keeping him to their right.
t.6.4.44: The royal sage Triśaṅku, the eminent forefather of us, the great-souled Ikṣvākus, shines spotless together with his family priest.
t.6.4.45: And the two Viśākhā stars shine forth, spotless and free from affliction; that is the supreme constellation of us, the great-souled Ikṣvākus.
t.6.4.46: The asterism of Nirṛti, the constellation of the Nairṛtas, is afflicted; Mūla, touched by a firmly rooted comet, is wrapped in its smoke.
t.6.4.47: And all this has come about for the destruction of the rākṣasas; at this time, for those seized by Kāla, their constellation is afflicted by a planet.
t.6.4.48: The waters are clear and sweet-tasting, the woods are laden with fruit, fragrances waft forth more abundantly, and the trees bear blossoms according to their season.
t.6.4.49: O lord, the monkey armies, drawn up in battle array, shine forth exceedingly, like the armies of the gods in the battle over Tārakā.
t.6.4.50: "Thus, noble one, having observed these signs, you ought to be glad." So the joyful Saumitri spoke, having comforted his brother.
t.6.4.51: Then the mighty army marched on, covering the whole earth, filled with tigers among bears and monkeys, whose weapons were their claws and fangs.
t.6.4.52: The earthly dust raised by the monkeys with the tips of their hands and the tips of their feet veiled the world, shutting out the radiance of the sun.
t.6.4.53: That mighty army of monkeys, thrilled and jubilant, protected by Sugrīva, marched on day and night.
t.6.4.54: All the vānaras, rejoicing in battle, went swiftly onward, eager to set Sītā free; nowhere did they rest even for a moment.
t.6.4.55: Then they reached Mount Sahya, crowded with trees and teeming with animals of many kinds, and the mountain Malaya as well.
t.6.4.56: Rāma went on his way, beholding as he went the wondrous forests, the rivers and the mountain streams of Sahya and of Malaya.
t.6.4.57: The monkeys broke down campaka, tilaka and mango trees, aśokas and sinduvārakas, karavīras and timiśas.
t.6.4.58: There the vānaras, swelling with strength, ate the fruits of the trees, fragrant as amṛta, along with their roots and flowers.
t.6.4.59: Those joyful monkeys, tawny as honey, went on their way drinking the hanging stores of honey, each as much as a droṇa in measure.
t.6.4.60: Breaking down the trees and likewise dragging away the creepers, and shattering the great mountains, the foremost of the monkeys marched onward.
t.6.4.61: Some monkeys, roaring and intoxicated with honey, leap down from the trees, while others climb up into the trees, and still others tumble down.
t.6.4.62: The earth became filled with those bulls among monkeys, just as the earth is covered with fields of ripened lotuses.
t.6.4.63: Then, having reached Mount Mahendra, the mighty-armed, lotus-eyed Rāma ascended its summit, adorned with trees.
t.6.4.64: Then Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, having climbed a peak, beheld the ocean, teeming with tortoises and fish.
t.6.4.65: Having crossed the Sahya and the great mountain Malaya, they reached in due order the ocean with its terrible roar.
t.6.4.66: Having descended, Rāma, the best of those who give delight, together with Sugrīva and with Lakṣmaṇa, went swiftly to the unsurpassed forest on the seashore.
t.6.4.67: Then, having reached the broad shore, whose rocky surface was washed by masses of water suddenly rising up, Rāma spoke these words.
t.6.4.68: Here we have arrived, O Sugrīva, at the abode of Varuṇa. Now, here, that anxious deliberation arises which had not arisen before.
t.6.4.69: From here onward lies this ocean, the lord of rivers, whose farther shore is far away; and this sea cannot be crossed without some means.
t.6.4.70: Therefore let our encampment be right here, and let counsel be taken here as to how this army of vānaras may reach the farther shore.
t.6.4.71: Thus the mighty-armed Rāma, worn down by the abduction of Sītā, having reached the ocean, then gave orders to make camp.
t.6.4.73: Having heard Rāma's words, Sugrīva, together with Lakṣmaṇa, encamped the army on the shore of the ocean, which was thick with trees.
t.6.4.72: The time has come for us to take counsel here about crossing the ocean. Let no one abandon his own troop and go off anywhere. Let brave vānaras go forth, for any hidden danger to us must be found out.
t.6.4.74: That army, stationed close to the ocean, shone resplendent like a second splendid ocean whose waters were the pale tawny hue of honey.
t.6.4.76: That army of monkeys, having reached the great ocean, was filled with joy as it gazed upon the great ocean tossed about by the force of the wind.
t.6.4.75: Then, having reached the forest along the shore, those bulls among the monkeys encamped there, longing for the farther shore of the great ocean.
t.6.4.77: Gazing upon the abode of Varuṇa, whose farther shore lay far away, vast and unconfined, and frequented by hosts of rākṣasas, the leaders of the monkey troops sat down.
t.6.4.78: They beheld the dreadful ocean, haunted by fierce crocodiles and seizing sea-monsters, heaving at the onset of night as the day waned and the moon rose, and crowded with countless reflections of the moon.
t.6.4.79: The abode of Varuṇa was strewn with huge sea-beasts swift as fierce winds and with timis and timiṃgilas, as though it were crowded with serpents whose coils were blazing.
t.6.4.81: Penetrated by crocodiles and the coils of serpents and tossed about by the wind, the swelling masses of water rose up and fell down.
t.6.4.80: They gazed upon that fathomless abode of the asuras, entered by mighty creatures and crowded with many mountains, hard to approach, a stronghold without any path.
t.6.4.82: They beheld the ocean, which looked like scattered sparks of fire, its shining waters full of great serpents, the dreadful domain of the foes of the gods, ever perilous with the depths of Pātāla.
t.6.4.83: The ocean looked like the sky, and the sky resembled the ocean; ocean and sky appeared without any distinction between them.
t.6.4.84: For the water seemed blended with the sky, and the sky blended with the water; both appeared alike in form, thronged with stars and gems.
t.6.4.86: Striking against one another and clinging together, the waves of the lord of rivers roared with a terrible sound, like great kettledrums in battle.
t.6.4.85: Between the two, the sky with its massed clouds risen up and the ocean heaving with rows of waves, there was no difference.
t.6.4.88: Those great-souled ones beheld the ocean, a reservoir of waters lashed by the wind, tossed up by the gale into the sky as though leaping with its waves, roaring with its whirling waves and waters, and heaving restlessly.
t.6.4.87: They beheld the ocean, its jewel-laden waters roaring, as if gripped by the wind, as if leaping up in anger, and teeming with hosts of sea creatures.
